text:
We piloted an AI note-taker with our field sales team for one quarter. Here's what we learned.

**1. Time came back.** Reps cut post-call admin by about 40%. That meant more prep for the next visit, not just earlier dinners.

**2. CRM data got better.** Notes were consistent, so managers could finally spot patterns in objections and competitor mentions.

**3. Trust took work.** Some customers hesitated. Reps who asked consent up front, and explained why, saw almost no pushback.

**4. Summaries aren't strategy.** The tool captured what was said. Reps still had to decide what mattered.

**5. Coaching shifted.** Managers reviewed real conversations instead of recollections.

We're keeping it, with clearer consent scripts.

What surprised your team most when adopting AI tools?

*(Synthetic scenario; figures are illustrative.)*
